final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mostly narrowed the claim to fit the existing record. That reframing is more accurate than the broader certification theory, but it does not resolve the core compliance gap. A caveated position can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat is policy-bounded and the required predicate is satisfied despite the limitation. Here the caveat identifies an unresolved predicate instead: a potentially material named-use-case weakness, open legal review, and no evidence of approved disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, certification may be arguable as a business readiness decision, but compliance is still not evidentially established under the release policy. The remaining issue is not tone or overstatement; it is missing policy-satisfying evidence.
remaining_concerns: The fraud dispute review segment misses target and is named in two bank pilot commitments, which fits the policy's materiality trigger for a named launch use case.
The legal review on whether that gap must be disclosed remains open, so the required compliance predicate is unresolved on the present record.
No admissible evidence shows an approved pre-launch disclosure or an approved risk acceptance covering this named-use-case limitation.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not satisfy the separate disclosure condition for a material named use case.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring, but they do not substitute for the internal policy requirement.
